title: Unbounded winding is the only difficulty in the cut-and-glue approach
body:
## The statement

In the cut-and-glue approach, the unboundedness of the winding around gamma is the *only*
difficulty.

## The proof, or where to find it

It suffices to keep track of the vector of incoming and outgoing arc pairs together with
the degree along gamma. Enough of the data to reconstruct the Euler characteristic and
the degree of the surface is determined by that finite amount of data.

This is worth stating positively and separately from the obstruction it refers to: it says
the problem is finite-dimensional apart from one unbounded parameter, and so identifies
precisely what would have to be controlled for the approach to go through.

**Status: this is a theorem, modulo the train-track scl technology of the cited paper of
Calegari and Walker. The derivation has not been written out.** It is not folklore in the
sense of being unproved; it is a routine consequence for somebody who knows that machinery.
But nobody has written it down, and until somebody does, this record will display as
"proof not written out" rather than as proved in the literature -- which is accurate.

**This is an invitation.** Writing out the derivation is a well-defined, self-contained
task, and whoever does it should publish an `argument` record supporting this one, or
supersede this record with one linked to the write-up by `proved_in`. It is a good first
contribution: the result is known to be true, so the risk is low, and the payoff is that
everything downstream of the cut-and-glue approach stops resting on an assertion.
